option_relations.rationale: Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) is a neurodegenerative disorder, but it is not directly related to Progressive supranuclear palsy, which is a distinct parkinsonian syndrome.

Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis–Frontotemporal Dementia (ALS-FTD) is a specific neurodegenerative disorder with features of both ALS and FTD. It is not directly related to Progressive supranuclear palsy.
Frontotemporal lobar degeneration–motor neuron disease (FTLD-MND) is a spectrum of disorders that includes ALS-FTD. It is not directly related to Progressive supranuclear palsy.

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-frontotemporal dementia (ALS-FTD) spectrum disorder (TBK1-related) specifies a genetic cause for ALS-FTD. This is a distinct neurodegenerative condition and not related to Progressive supranuclear palsy.
